title: Conversations — The Midnight Train
subtitle: Two strangers in a dimly lit carriage discover they share the same memory.
subheading: Episode I: Two strangers in a dimly lit carriage discover they share the same memory.
author: Terminal Musing

content.text: [Setting: A second-class passenger coach on the night train departing Warsaw for Vienna. Rain lashes against the double-paned window. A single overhead amber bulb flickers rhythmically with the rocking of the bogies.]
[Characters: JULIAN, late thirties, coat buttoned to the chin, nursing an unread paperback. ELENA, sixties, woolen scarf, notebook resting across her knees.]
JULIAN: (Without looking up) If you turn the page any slower, the ink will evaporate.

ELENA: (A brief pause, pencil suspended) When you reach my age, young man, you learn that sentences are not sprint tracks. They are rooms. You don't run through a room you might never be invited into again.
JULIAN: (Closes his book with a soft thump) What room are you in right now?
ELENA: A corridor, actually. Painted pale green. Smelling of wet wool and cheap floor wax. A telephone on the wall with a broken dial that only rings when someone is already too late.
JULIAN: (Stiffens slightly; looks directly at her) Number 14 Prusa Street.
ELENA: (Looks up slowly for the first time. The train enters a tunnel; in the black reflection of the window, their faces overlap.) How do you know the number?
JULIAN: Because my grandfather lived on the third floor. And he spent twenty-four years waiting for a telephone call from that exact corridor.
ELENA: (A long, breathless silence. The wheels click-clack beneath the floorboards.) Then your name is Julian.
ELENA: (She shuts her notebook gently.) Tell the conductor when he comes that I gave you my ticket. I won't be needing the return.
